title: After the necklace is lost
body:
Read the summary of this part of the story and answer the questions that follow.

When Matilda discovered that the diamond necklace was gone, she and her husband searched the folds of her dress and cloak and every pocket. Loisel then retraced on foot the way they had walked. Next, he went to the police and to the cab offices, and he put an advertisement in the newspapers offering a reward. He asked Matilda to write to Mme Forestier that she had broken the clasp and was having it repaired, so that they would have time. After a week, with all hope gone, they decided to replace the jewel. In a shop of the Palais-Royal they found a chaplet of diamonds that looked exactly like the lost one. It was valued at forty thousand francs, but they could get it for thirty-six thousand. Loisel had eighteen thousand francs that his father had left him; he borrowed the rest from usurers and other lenders, making ruinous promises. When Matilda returned the necklace, Mme Forestier did not open the box, and Matilda wondered whether her friend would take her for a robber if she noticed the substitution.
